name: Iraq

flag.description: Three equal horizontal stripes of red, white and black, with the phrase "Allahu akbar" written in green Kufic script in the centre of the white stripe.
flag.symbolism: The Pan-Arab colours are commonly said to represent courage (red), generosity (white) and past oppression (black); the inscription is the Takbir, "God is the greatest".

hook: Iraq writes green Arabic script on the white stripe; Egypt has a gold eagle, Yemen's stripes are bare, and Syria now uses green-white-black with red stars.
trivia: Until 2008 the flag carried three green stars, which were removed in that year's redesign.
The Takbir was added in 1991 in a handwritten style; the current flag uses a standardised Kufic script instead.
